findings.title: The Check operation exhibits asymmetric cache trust logic: cached permission grants are trusted and returned immediately
findings.description: The Check operation exhibits asymmetric cache trust logic: cached permission grants are trusted and returned immediately, but cached denials from the same permission cache are ignored, leading to a fresh database lookup. This allows stale cached grants to provide access to revoked resources, posing a security risk.

adjudication.why: Cached grants were already trusted in getUserPermissions/getAnonymousPermissions. The new path refreshes a denial from the permission map, while the separate permission-denial cache explicitly short-circuits to false; the label does not establish a new stale-grant regression.

findings.description: The test comment says the cached permissions 'allow access', but the map stores false for dashboards:uid:dash1, so checkPermission will still treat this scope as not allowed.

adjudication.why: The false-valued test seed does not exercise the intended cached-grant override. This is a coverage-only gold item, not a production behavior defect; review excludes missing test coverage. The old candidate did surface it.
